newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 2.26 pct lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 2.26 pct lower on profit taking.

text.p: Thai stocks on Tuesday to finish sharply lower as nerves ahead of a release of key economic data on Thursday saw investors take profits on blue chips after recent sharp gains, analysts said.
The SET Index finished 11.40 points, or 2.26 percent lower to 493.13. The SET 50 dipped 0.96 points or 2.68 percent to 34.92 in trade worth 5.12 billion baht.

"After technical gains that has seen the market rise some 50 points, I think people were taking profits especiually since the fundamentals are unchanged," said Tanawat Patchimkul, an analyst at Seamico Securities Plc.
Following substantial central bank intervention to defend the currency in May, investors were warily awaiting foreign reserves data and other economic indicators, traders said.

Decrees easing foreign ownership restrictions on Thai finance firms on a discretionary basis which emerged late in the afternoon failed to revive the market as investors believed the move, though positive, could take time to bring benefits.
"It seems like a pretty good move on paper ... but it could be a long and drawn out process," said a finance sector analyst at a major European brokerage.

"It remains to be seen which ones they'll give approval to. If they just approve the worst ones then the question arises as to what price and to the extent to which the central bank is prepared to help take on a firm's poor assets," he added.

Assets quaility and liquidity concerns surrounding finance firms saw the sector sink 5.81 percent on Tuesday. Banks ended 4.29 percent lower. Although communications stocks posted a 0.72 percent gain, they to were subject to late profit taking.
Bangkok Bank Plc finished five baht lower at 114 Thai Farmres Bank Plc dipped 4.50 baht to 78 and Advanced Info Service Plc added five to 162.
